examples.scenario: Cell center lies exactly on parcel boundary and contains returns false.
examples.reason: Contains excludes boundary-only membership.

examples.scenario: Cell center lies on boundary and covers returns true.
examples.reason: Covers explicitly includes boundary points.

examples.scenario: contains and covers disagree but code keeps whichever ran first.
examples.reason: Membership predicate must be predetermined.

examples.scenario: contains_properly is used for parcel membership.
examples.reason: It rejects common boundary points by definition.

examples.scenario: Touch-only cell is treated as interior.
examples.reason: Touches and interior overlap are different topological relations.

examples.scenario: DE-9IM matrix differs between primary and replay.
examples.reason: Predicate agreement without relation-matrix agreement is insufficient.

examples.scenario: Prepared geometry returns a different membership set.
examples.reason: Preparation may optimize but must not alter predicate semantics.

examples.scenario: Self-intersecting parcel polygon is rasterized directly.
examples.reason: Invalid polygon topology cannot define canonical membership.

examples.scenario: Invalidity reason is omitted from rejection record.
examples.reason: Failure provenance must identify the topology defect.

examples.scenario: make_valid runs automatically with no manifest entry.
examples.reason: Repair can alter geometry structure.

examples.scenario: linework and structure make-valid outputs differ.
examples.reason: Repair method belongs in provenance.

examples.scenario: Repaired polygon becomes MultiPolygon and code keeps only first part.
examples.reason: Repair output type and all parts must be preserved.

examples.scenario: Repair collapses part of geometry to a line and line is treated as parcel area.
examples.reason: Lower-dimensional repair output cannot silently define area membership.

examples.scenario: Point lies inside a polygon hole but is counted as parcel interior.
examples.reason: Interior rings exclude area.

examples.scenario: Point lies exactly on hole boundary.
examples.reason: Hole boundary semantics must follow the same explicit topology rule.

examples.scenario: MultiPolygon second component is ignored.
examples.reason: All polygon components belong to canonical geometry.

examples.scenario: Ring direction changes and geometry is considered different business shape.
examples.reason: Ring orientation can be canonicalized without changing polygon semantics.

examples.scenario: Geometry coordinate order differs but normalized geometry is equal.
examples.reason: Coordinate ordering alone is not semantic membership.

examples.scenario: Precision grid changes from 0 to 0.01 m between runs.
examples.reason: Coordinate rounding may alter topology and membership.

examples.scenario: Pointwise precision reduction creates self-intersection.
examples.reason: Pointwise reduction does not guarantee valid topology.

examples.scenario: Narrow polygon component collapses after precision reduction.
examples.reason: Collapsed geometry changes membership domain.

examples.scenario: Intersection replay uses a different grid_size.
examples.reason: Grid size affects shared geometry.

examples.scenario: Center-based rasterization is compared with ALL_TOUCHED output as if equivalent.
examples.reason: They select different cell sets.

examples.scenario: ALL_TOUCHED is enabled only in one replay.
examples.reason: Membership policy must match exactly.

examples.scenario: Fractional coverage cells are converted to binary using an undocumented threshold.
examples.reason: Fractional and binary membership are distinct policies.

examples.scenario: Polygon just touches a pixel center under default GDAL rasterization.
examples.reason: GDAL documents this edge behavior as unspecified.

examples.scenario: Feature order changes under ALL_TOUCHED and edge value changes.
examples.reason: Input order can affect touching-edge burn results.

examples.scenario: Nested polygon inversion runs without GEOS support.
examples.reason: GDAL requires GEOS for correct nested inverse results.

examples.scenario: Bounding-box cells are treated as polygon members.
examples.reason: Bounding box is only a coarse candidate filter.

examples.scenario: A Z coordinate changes but XY boundary is identical.
examples.reason: GEOS validity/membership topology is 2D here.

examples.scenario: Mask exclusion is encoded as if it were polygon exclusion.
examples.reason: Raster validity and parcel topology are independent filters.

examples.scenario: NODATA exclusion changes parcel membership count.
examples.reason: A member cell may still be invalid raster data.

examples.scenario: Cell row/column differs but world center is rounded to same text coordinate.
examples.reason: Row/column identity prevents coordinate-rounding collisions.

examples.scenario: Two cells share center coordinates due to incorrect affine replay.
examples.reason: Membership requires unique correct pixel addressing.

examples.scenario: Membership set count matches but one cell differs.
examples.reason: Cardinality alone does not prove identical membership.

examples.scenario: Membership set is serialized in traversal order.
examples.reason: Traversal order must not change digest.

examples.scenario: Boundary-touch set is omitted from ledger.
examples.reason: Touch-only cells explain covers/contains differences.

examples.scenario: Hole-excluded set is not recorded.
examples.reason: Hole topology must be replayable.

examples.scenario: Primary covers set and independent covers set differ by one cell.
examples.reason: Canonical membership must match exactly.

examples.scenario: Primary DE-9IM and independent DE-9IM classify a boundary point differently.
examples.reason: Topological relation drift blocks terminal use.

examples.scenario: Normalized geometry digest differs despite equal area.
examples.reason: Equal area does not prove equal boundary.

examples.scenario: Geometry bytes match but CRS differs.
examples.reason: Same coordinates under different CRS do not define same parcel.

examples.scenario: CRS matches but precision-grid metadata differs.
examples.reason: Precision model affects topology operations.

examples.scenario: Coverage neighbours overlap along a sliver.
examples.reason: Exact-edge polygon coverage should not overlap.

examples.scenario: Narrow gap exists between parcel coverage edges.
examples.reason: Gap detection can identify nonmatching coverage edges.

examples.scenario: Coverage hole is automatically treated as invalid gap.
examples.reason: Valid polygon coverage may contain holes.

examples.scenario: Exterior/interior ring orientation is used to override explicit hole structure.
examples.reason: Orientation is normalization, not a replacement for shell/hole structure.

examples.scenario: Polygonize diagonal connectivity setting is reused as parcel membership semantics.
examples.reason: Raster-region connectivity is distinct from vector boundary membership.

examples.scenario: Prepared geometry cache survives geometry mutation.
examples.reason: Prepared state belongs to the geometry version it indexed.

examples.scenario: Exact membership is computed before geometry validity check.
examples.reason: Invalid source geometry cannot define canonical set.

examples.scenario: Extrema are computed before exact parcel membership.
examples.reason: Only exact member cells can enter extrema.

examples.scenario: A fixture polygon proves topology behavior and its member cells are copied to production.
examples.reason: Examples validate logic only.

examples.scenario: Static topology tests pass and target numeric elevations are emitted.
examples.reason: Canonical runtime boundary is not bound.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but parcel geometry is guessed from nearby fixture.
examples.reason: Target geometry must come from canonical execution.

examples.scenario: Exact boundary runtime rows are marked complete without runner output.
examples.reason: No runtime evidence exists while ACK is absent.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution remains BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second topology runner is launched.
examples.reason: Continuation contract permits only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 readiness is reported as boundary accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation readiness is not measured parcel-boundary accuracy.

examples.scenario: Membership digest matches but underlying geometry digest differs.
examples.reason: One target window can match accidentally despite geometry drift.

examples.scenario: Batch 87 is reported as final height difference.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM and runtime sampling remain required.
